conventions.convention: The horizon n≥1, action count k>1, and expert count M>1 are integers. Rewards in [0,1]^k and stochastic advice rows are deterministic and fixed before learner randomization; advice is revealed before the current action.

Expected regret is the expectation of the best fixed expert's cumulative advice-weighted reward minus the learner's cumulative observed reward. The comparator is nonrandom because the instance is fixed.

Exp4 starts with uniform expert weights, uses exact real arithmetic and η>0, and assumes a probability space carrying the prescribed measurable finite action draws. No sampler construction or uniform exploration mixture is required.

An importance-weighted quotient on an action with P(t,i)=0 is defined to be zero on every outcome. Its action reward estimate is therefore one; no componentwise unbiasedness is asserted for unsupported actions.
The theorem uses the natural logarithm and the positive learning rate η=√(2 log M/(nk)); its regret guarantee is for this tuned rate.

load_bearing.statement: For n≥1, k>1, M>1 and η>0 in the fixed contextual bandit protocol, initialize Q(1,m)=1/M, mix advice using P(t,i)=Σm Q(t,m)E(t)(m,i), sample an action with conditional distribution P(t), form the specified importance-weighted reward estimates with zero quotient on unsupported actions, and normalize Q(t,m) exp(η times the expert reward estimate) to obtain Q(t+1,m).

For every exact-real Exp4 input with n≥1, k>1, M>1, finite η>0, an oblivious reward/advice instance and supplied measurable draws, every Q_t is a strictly positive probability vector, P_t belongs to Δ_k, and P(t,i)=0 implies E(t)(m,i)=0 for every expert. All estimates are finite, corresponding estimated losses are nonnegative, normalization is finite and positive, and the procedure completes all n rounds.

In Exp4, at every round t∈[n] and for every expert m∈[M], the conditional expectation of the expert reward estimate given the pre-action history equals ⟨E(t)_m,x_t⟩. This includes zero-probability actions, without asserting componentwise unbiasedness on unsupported actions.

At every Exp4 round, with estimated expert loss equal to one minus estimated expert reward, the conditional expectation of Σm Q(t,m) times the squared estimated expert loss is at most k, including zero-probability actions under the zero-quotient convention.

For any Exp4 run with η>0 and any fixed expert m*, every realized action sequence satisfies: the cumulative estimated reward of m* minus the cumulative Q-weighted estimated expert reward is at most log M/η plus (η/2) times the cumulative Q-weighted squared estimated expert loss.

For integers n≥1, k>1, M>1, deterministic rewards x_t∈[0,1]^k and stochastic advice rows fixed before learner randomization, with advice revealed before action and only sampled rewards observed, Exp4 with η=√(2 log M/(nk)) has expected regret against the best fixed expert at most √(2nk log M).

seams_checked.note: Checked the prerequisite page inventory and the actual estimator, conditional-moment and nonpositive-axis exponential suppliers against their uses in Exp4. The general estimator requires positive probability on every arm; Exp4 explicitly identifies its positive-coordinate use, defines zero quotients locally, and proves that unsupported actions receive zero advice from every expert. Its finite-history calculations establish the needed moments directly. The exponential bound is applied only to nonpositive arguments. No exploration-based Exp3 guarantee or stronger adversary scope is imported.
